items.title: Man first cited as witness, later made accused: Delhi court says ED's conduct disturbing, seeks report
items.summary: A Delhi court recently took strong exception to the manner in which the Enforcement Directorate (ED) proceeded to a make a person an accused in a money laundering after he was first cited as a witness. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Dheeraj Mor of the Patiala House Court noted that the investigating officer (IO) of ED who first probed the case had cited one Mr. MSA as a witness in a money laundering case. However, the officer who replaced the first officer made Mr.A an accused and arrested him. The court termed such incongruities as disturbing. "The glaring and disturbing aspect of this case is required to be noted. The hallmark of investigation is its objectivity. Subjective interpretation of IO must be deprecated as it would make a supposed objective investigation dependent upon his uncontrolled whims and fancies," the Court said. In view of the above, it ordered the ED Director to conduct an inquiry against the two investigating officers (IO). items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.
